newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: Lithuanian PM plans energy, transport firm sales.
newsitem.headline: Lithuanian PM plans energy, transport firm sales.

text.p: New Lithuanian Prime Minister Gediminas Vagnorius on Thursday said that the government would draw up a new list of companies for privatisation in 1997 that would include the airline and energy firms.
But he added that the state was unlikely to sell more than 50 percent of the shares in these key companies.
Vagnorius said the government also intended to organise open tenders for the privatisations.
"No company included in the 1997 privatisation list will sell more than 50 percent of the state-owned shares," he told a news conference.

The government's wish-list of companies to be privatised includes large energy and transport firms such as Mazheikiu Nafta refinery, companies in the port of Klaipeda, Lithuanian Airlines and the multi-storey Lietuva hotel in Vilnius.
The 12 biggest companies are to be privatised first with the help of international aid and foreign companies.
Vagnorius also said that his government wants to strengthen the banking sector by privatising some state-owned banks.
"We would like to sell them, especially the ones facing problems, to foreign banks," Vagnorius added.
Lithuania's privatisation programme became bogged down in its second stage after a successful first-round sale of apartments and small businesses.
But unlike neighbours Latvia and Estonia, no moves have been made to sell the telecommunications or transport companies that would appeal most to foreign investors and need modernising.
Vagnorius has already committed the government to selling the state-owned telecommunications company.
